title: Detection of Comorbidities in Monogenic Male Infertility
author: van der Heijden, G W
materials: Both men were referred to the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology of the Radboud University Medical Center with their partner with a wish to conceive. Prior knowledge of male cause for infertility was present based on a semen analysis elsewhere. Briefly, the andrological work-up is performed by a trained andrology specialist and consists of a semen analyses, an endocrine evaluation, assessment of the urological history, assessment of the urogenital tract (scrotum’s form, presence and consistency of the testes, epididymis and vas deferens, form and length of the penis, and position of the meatus). When indicated (anomaly of vas deferens) a sonogram of the kidneys is performed. Furthermore, potential problems with micturition, sexological issues, and pain in the genital region are discussed.

Immunological tests were performed in routine and specialized diagnostics laboratory of the Radboudumc (ISO15189 accredited). Total IgG, IgA, IgM, and IgD were measured using turbidimetry on a Cobas 6000 (Roche, Basel, Switzerland). Measurements were performed according to manufacturer guidelines. Total IgE was measured on an Immunocap 250 (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Uppsala, Sweden). IgG subclasses were measured using nephelometry on an Atellica (Siemens Healthineers, Erlangen, Germany). Antinuclear antibody profiling was performed with indirect immunofluorescence on Hep-2 cells (Inova Diagnostics, San Diego, USA). M-protein screening was performed with serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation electrophoresis on a Hydrasys2 (Sebia, Lisses, France). Immune-phenotyping analysis was performed on fresh EDTA blood by using flow cytometry as previously described (Huys et al., 2022). Briefly, the frequencies and absolute counts of the main lymphocyte subsets (CD3+ total T cells, CD3+CD4+ T-helper cells, CD3+CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, CD19+ B cells, and CD3-CD56+ NK cells) were determined using an automated Aquios Tetra assay (Beckman Coulter, Woerden, The Netherlands). In addition, the activation, differentiation, and subset composition of T cells, B cells, and NK cells were evaluated using validated laboratory-developed tests on cells subjected to bulk lysis followed by specific stainings and measurement on a Navios flow cytometer (Beckman Coulter). Data were analyzed with Kaluza software (Beckman Coulter).

steps.title: Assemble multidisciplinary medical team
steps.instruction: Gather the required professionals – two clinical geneticists, a certified urologist (European Association of Andrology), a reproductive‑medicine gynecologist, a clinical laboratory geneticist (European Board of Medical Genetics), and two senior clinical embryologists (European Society of Human Reproduction and Embryology) – to form the multidisciplinary medical team (MMT) that will guide protocol development.

steps.title: Perform standard genetic diagnostic work‑up
steps.instruction: Run an exome‑sequencing‑based gene panel that includes only genes with an established gene‑disease relationship; interpret variants according to ACMG/AMP guidelines, retaining only likely pathogenic or pathogenic calls. For recessive findings, perform segregation analysis to confirm compound heterozygosity. If a variant of unknown significance (VUS) is identified, order additional investigations (e.g., semen analysis, testis histology) to aid re‑classification.

steps.title: Conduct comprehensive andrological evaluation
steps.instruction: Have a trained andrology specialist perform semen analysis, endocrine profiling, and a detailed urological history. Examine the urogenital tract (scrotal form, testes consistency, epididymis, vas deferens, penile length and shape, meatus position). If vas deferens anomalies are noted, obtain a renal sonogram. Discuss micturition problems, sexual issues, and genital‑region pain with the patient.

steps.title: Curate gene expression and comorbidity data
steps.instruction: Query the Human Protein Atlas (HPA) for the gene of interest, extracting tissues from the “tissue RNA expression” tab and cell types from the “cell type RNA expression” tab that show ≥4‑fold higher expression than the mean across all tissues/cell types. List reported comorbidities from OMIM, group those with a shared underlying cause, and discard organs lacking HPA data or congenital conditions.

substeps.instruction: Open the HPA portal and locate the ‘Summary’ tab.
Record all tissues under ‘Tissue specificity’ and all cell types under ‘Single cell type specificity’ that meet the 4‑fold cut‑off.
Retrieve OMIM entries for the gene, note all comorbidities, and merge overlapping categories.

steps.title: Perform immunological laboratory testing
steps.instruction: In the ISO15189‑accredited laboratory, measure the following on the patient’s serum or fresh EDTA blood:

substeps.instruction: Total IgG, IgA, IgM, and IgD by turbidimetry on a Cobas 6000 (Roche).
Total IgE on an Immunocap 250 (Thermo Fisher).
IgG subclasses by nephelometry on an Atellica (Siemens Healthineers).
Antinuclear antibodies by indirect immunofluorescence on Hep‑2 cells (Inova Diagnostics).
M‑protein screening via serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation on a Hydrasys2 (Sebia).
Lymphocyte subset frequencies and absolute counts (CD3+ T cells, CD3+CD4+ T‑helper, CD3+CD8+ cytotoxic, CD19+ B cells, CD3‑CD56+ NK cells) using an automated Aquios Tetra assay (Beckman Coulter).
Activation, differentiation, and subset composition of T, B, and NK cells using laboratory‑developed bulk‑lysis staining protocols measured on a Navios flow cytometer (Beckman Coulter).
Analyze flow data with Kaluza software (Beckman Coulter).

steps.title: Perform comprehensive ophthalmologic assessment
steps.instruction: During a single‑day visit, evaluate both eyes with the following sequence:

substeps.instruction: Color vision using the Hardy–Rand–Rittler test.
Refraction measurement followed by best‑corrected visual acuity on a 4‑m ETDRS chart.
Axial length measurement with an IOLMaster 700 (Carl Zeiss Meditec).
Slit‑lamp fundoscopy.
Fundus photography with a Topcon DRI OCT Triton.
Fundus autofluorescence and spectral‑domain OCT (dense volume scan: 30° × 25°, 241 sections, ART = 9, high resolution) on a Heidelberg Spectralis.
Static perimetry on an Octopus 900 (Haag‑Streit) using EyeSuite v i8.2.2.0/perimetry v3.6.1 and the OP3/32 Dynamic White‑White protocol.
Electroretinography on an Espion e3 system (Diagnosys) with DTL electrodes: scotopic (V5), photopic (V6.1), and multifocal (61 hexagons) recordings per ISCEV standards.
Dark‑adaptation testing on the same system.
Adaptive optics imaging (AO‑FIO, ImagineEyes) to assess photoreceptor mosaic and cone density.

steps.title: Fix and embed sperm cells for ultrastructure
steps.instruction: Process washed spermatozoa for electron microscopy as follows:

substeps.instruction: Fix overnight in 2 % glutaraldehyde prepared in 0.1 M Na‑cacodylate buffer.
Wash in the same cacodylate buffer, then fix for 1 h in 2 % osmium tetroxide (OsO₄).
Pellet the cells, embed in agar, dehydrate through graded alcohols, and infiltrate with Epon resin.
Polymerize the resin, cut ultrathin sections of 60 nm thickness, and collect on 200‑mesh copper grids.

steps.title: Finalize gene‑specific phenotyping protocol
steps.instruction: Collate the expression data, literature findings, and clinical test results; present them to the MMT for consensus; identify and contact relevant clinical experts; incorporate expert‑suggested targeted questions and additional tests; and produce the finalized gene‑specific phenotyping protocol ready for patient application.

substeps.instruction: Create a summary table of high‑expression tissues/cell types and associated comorbidities (Step 1‑2).
Prepare a concise report for the MMT meeting (Step 3).
Reach agreement on priority tissues, questions, and tests (Step 4‑6).
Document the agreed‑upon questionnaire, HPO terms, and test panels (Step 7).
